newsitem.title: UK: Britain's jobless drops to six-year low in December.
newsitem.headline: Britain's jobless drops to six-year low in December.

text.p: British unemployment fell to a six-year low of 1.88 million workers in December and the jobless rate dipped to 6.7 percent, the Office for National Statistics said Wednesday.

The larger than expected seasonally adjusted fall of 45,100 in the jobless register reflected robust economic activity, but steady growth in November average earnings showed this was still not being reflected in rising wage costs.
The figures were welcomed by the Conservative government, which is anxious to highlight any good economic news to improve its prospects in the forthcoming election, due by May.

"Unemployment is falling right across the country and the smile on Britain's face can broaden," Prime Minister John Major said. "In the last four years, Britain has created more jobs than all the other major countries of Europe put together."
The ONS said the number of unemployed people stood at 26.076 million at the end of the third quarter, a rise of 299,000 compared with a year earlier.
The statistics office said underlying average earnings rose 4 percent in the year to November, the same rate as in the previous month.
Unit wage costs were up 4.2 percent in the three months to November compared with a year earlier.
The office said special factors had inflated the drop in unemployment in December, which followed a dramatic 95,400 fall in November.

The introduction of a new jobseekers' allowance, under which people receive unemployment benefit only if they can prove they are actively seeking work, may have accounted for up to 10,000 of the fall in December.
